alt.name: 2019 Nissan Altima 2.5 SV
alt.vline: Everyone avoids this car for the wrong reason.
alt.vsub: The Altima's CVT reputation is real — it just belongs to the previous generation. We read all 226 NHTSA complaints filed against the 2019: roughly five mention the transmission at all. Fifty-two are electrical. Forty-eight are the engine. You've been worrying about the wrong thing, and the actual problems are still sitting right here.

risks.t: Engine — overheating, coolant, metal in the oil
risks.b: The second-largest complaint category and by far the most expensive one. Owners report overheating with hot air from the vents, EGR cooler and valve failures, cracked heads, and — in more than one filing — metal found in the oil pan.
e: 48 engine complaints on the 2019 model year, plus 18 more filed under engine cooling.
Recurring fault codes across filings: P0404 and P0101 (EGR and mass airflow), P0087 (fuel rail pressure).
At 149,000 miles, a cold-start coolant check and an oil inspection tell you more than the entire test drive will. Metal in the oil ends the conversation.

risks.t: Electrical — the most complained-about thing on this car
risks.b: Door lock actuators are the standout: owners report all four failing, leaving doors that won't lock or unlock by key or remote. Add repeat battery drain and an infotainment head unit that changes stations and volume on its own.
e: 52 electrical complaints — the largest single category for this model year.
None of this strands you. All of it is the kind of annoyance that makes people sell the car two years early, which is probably why this one is for sale.

risks.t: Seven open recalls — check them, they're free
risks.b: Including a fuel pump lock ring that can disengage on 2.5L front-drive cars (19V316000) and a fuel tube retainer clip (18V922000) — both fuel-leak fire risks. Also tires, brake light switch, and two separate backup camera campaigns.
e: Seven recall campaigns cover this model year. Recall 25V437000 (engine bearing failure and fire risk) applies to the 2.0L VC-Turbo only — not this 2.5L car.
Run the VIN through NHTSA before you go look at it. Unrepaired recalls are free to fix and give you something concrete to hold over the seller.

chk: Check the oil before you check anything else. Metal content shows up in NHTSA filings on this engine. Pull the dipstick yourself, in daylight.
Run the VIN for open recalls first. Seven campaigns cover this year, two of them fuel-leak fire risks. It's free, it takes a minute, and it's leverage.
Lock and unlock every door, twice. The single most-reported failure on this car, and the one the seller definitely knows about.
Decide your walk-away number before you go. The real question isn't whether $8,999 is cheap. It's whether losing $8,999 would ruin your year.

meta.title: 2019 Nissan Altima Problems: What 226 NHTSA Complaints Actually Say
meta.desc: Everyone blames the CVT. We read all 226 federal complaints filed against the 2019 Altima — about five mention the transmission. Here is what actually goes wrong, what it costs, and what to check before you buy.

f150.name: 2018 Ford F-150 XLT SuperCrew 3.5 EcoBoost
f150.vline: It's the transmission. Not the engine everyone warns you about.
f150.vsub: Every forum tells you to listen for cam phaser rattle on these. We pulled the NHTSA complaints for the 2018: seven of nine are the 10-speed transmission. One is the cam phasers. The internet has you checking the wrong thing in the driveway.

risks.t: 10R80 transmission — CDF clutch sleeve defect
risks.b: Owners describe violent shifting, RPM flaring, harsh unexpected downshifts at speed, and slipping. Filings repeatedly name the 10R80 CDF clutch-cylinder sleeve defect, which affects 2017–2022 trucks. Corrected parts reportedly weren't in Ford's supply until 2023.
e: 7 of 9 complaints for this model year are filed under Power Train, all describing the same shifting behaviour.
The 10R80 sleeve defect is documented across owner communities as a 2017–2022 issue rather than a one-off.
This is the test drive. Not the cold start. If it flares or slams on a downshift once, it will do it again, and the repair is real money.

risks.t: Cam phaser rattle — real, but not the headline
risks.b: A few seconds of rattle on a cold start. Well documented on these EcoBoost V6s and worth checking, but in the federal complaint data for this year it's a footnote next to the transmission.
e: One engine complaint for this model year mentions cam phaser work, and it's about a leaking repair rather than the original fault.
Ford revised the design; trucks repaired with updated parts generally stay fixed.
Still check it. Just don't let a clean cold start convince you the truck is fine — that's not where this one goes wrong.

risks.t: What it did for a living
risks.b: 81,000 miles of towing and 81,000 miles of commuting are not the same vehicle. The hitch, rear suspension and brakes will tell you which one this is.
e: A chewed-up hitch ball on a low-mileage truck says more than any history report.

chk: Drive it 30 minutes in mixed traffic and force downshifts. This is the whole inspection. The 10-speed misbehaves under load and deceleration, not on a smooth highway cruise.
Ask whether the transmission has been touched. Parts corrected for the sleeve defect only reached dealers around 2023 — anything repaired before that may be back.
Still start it stone cold and listen. Cam phasers are a smaller risk here, but it's five seconds of your time.
Get under the back of it. Hitch, wiring and rear brakes tell you how this truck actually lived.

meta.title: 2018 Ford F-150 Problems: It Is the Transmission, Not the Cam Phasers
meta.desc: Seven of nine NHTSA complaints against the 2018 F-150 are the 10R80 ten-speed transmission. One is cam phasers. Here is what to actually test on the drive, and what the repair costs.

rav.name: 2020 Toyota RAV4 XLE AWD
rav.vline: Still the smart buy. Just not the flawless one people assume.
rav.vsub: 627 complaints on the 2020, and the top category isn't the engine — it's the body. Liftgate hinges crack. There's a coolant bypass valve that goes around 60,000 to 100,000 miles and dealers charge $800–1,300 to fix. And an airbag sensor recall. It's still the best car on this page. Go in with your eyes open, not closed.

risks.t: Coolant bypass valve — the bill nobody warns you about
risks.b: A failing valve leaks coolant into electrical connectors and triggers an engine warning. It lands squarely in the mileage window this car is heading into, and owners report dealers charging full price for what many of them consider a design fault.
e: 61 engine complaints on the 2020, with this valve the recurring theme.
At 53,900 miles you are just short of the window. Price this in as a near-certain future bill rather than a maybe.

risks.t: Liftgate hinges crack — and it's the #1 complaint
risks.b: The largest single complaint category on this car is Structure, and it's almost entirely the rear hatch. Owners report hinges cracking, mounting points bending or fracturing, and hatches that no longer close properly.
e: 89 structure complaints — more than engine, airbags or electrical.
Open and close the tailgate a dozen times and look hard at the hinges. It's the easiest thing on this list to check and nobody does it.

risks.t: Airbag sensor recall 23V865000
risks.b: An occupant classification sensor defect that can stop the passenger airbag deploying in a crash. Owners have reported long waits for remedy parts. Six recalls total cover this model year.
e: Recall 23V865000 — occupant classification sensor. Five other campaigns cover fuel pump, frontal airbags, cooling, power steering and a front lower control arm.
Check the VIN and ask the dealer to confirm completion in writing. A recall you can't get fixed is still a recall.

chk: Work the tailgate a dozen times and inspect the hinges. The most-complained-about thing on this car, and a two-minute check almost nobody performs.
Run the VIN for all six recalls. Get written confirmation each is closed, especially the airbag sensor campaign.
Budget $1,000 for the coolant valve. This car is right at the edge of the window. It's not a reason to walk — it's a reason to negotiate.
Don't haggle yourself out of it. These sell fast and near asking for a reason. Losing this car over $500 would be the actual mistake.

meta.title: 2020 Toyota RAV4 Problems: 627 Complaints, and the Top One Is the Tailgate
meta.desc: The most-reported problem on the 2020 RAV4 is not the engine — it is cracked liftgate hinges. Plus a coolant valve that costs $800 to $1,300 and an airbag recall. Still a smart buy, with your eyes open.

x5.name: 2017 BMW X5 xDrive35i
x5.vline: You can afford this car. You cannot afford this car.
x5.vsub: Nothing here is unusual for a nine-year-old German SUV. But the most-complained-about item isn't the one the forums obsess over — it's the high-pressure fuel pump, and owners report it failing under 60,000 miles and leaving them stopped in traffic without warning. The $17,200 is the cover charge, not the bill.

risks.t: High-pressure fuel pump — sudden stall, no warning
risks.b: The single largest complaint category on this car. Owners describe abrupt power loss and stalling in traffic, with the whole high-pressure fuel system replaced. One filing documents two separate failures, at 39,066 and 57,376 miles.
e: 16 fuel and propulsion complaints on the 2017 X5 — more than any other category.
This is the one to actually worry about, and it's not what you'll read on the forums. Losing power in a live traffic lane is a different category of problem from a gasket weeping oil.

risks.t: Cooling system — water pump, fan, overheating
risks.b: Owners report overheating with a cluster of warning lights, and water pump failure around 62,000 miles. Radiator fan assembly faults appear repeatedly, including connector corrosion from liquid exposure.
e: 13 complaints under engine and engine cooling for this model year.
No record of the pump being replaced by 89,000 miles means treat it as a bill you've already run up and simply haven't been handed.

risks.t: Oil leaks — real, but forum-grade not federal-grade
risks.b: Valve cover and filter housing gaskets harden with heat and this engine is the age where both give up. Consistently reported by owners — though notably it barely registers in federal complaint data, because a slow leak isn't a safety issue.
e: One of the most consistently discussed items on this engine at this age and mileage.
We're labelling this owner-reported rather than NHTSA-verified on purpose. It's still very likely — but you should know which of these claims we can actually prove.

chk: Ask directly whether the high-pressure fuel pump has been replaced. It's the top complaint category and owners report failures well under 60,000 miles. This one can strand you.
Use a BMW specialist, not the shop down the road. $200 here is the best money in this entire transaction.
Ask for water pump and thermostat records. No paperwork at 89,000 miles means assume it's due and price it in.
Answer this honestly before you go: could you absorb a surprise $2,500 twice in the first year? If not, walk. There's no price that fixes this.

meta.title: 2017 BMW X5 Problems: The Fuel Pump Nobody Warns You About
meta.desc: Forums obsess over oil leaks. The top NHTSA complaint category on the 2017 X5 is the high-pressure fuel pump, with owners reporting sudden stalls under 60,000 miles. Full cost of ownership breakdown.

civic_2019.name: 2019 Honda Civic
civic_2019.vline: Nobody warns you about the steering. They should.
civic_2019.vsub: 348 complaints filed against the 2019 Civic, and the largest category by a distance is steering — 97 of them. Owners describe a wheel that sticks and refuses to self-centre at highway speed. Second is the fuel system at 78, most of it the recalled fuel pump. Neither is what the internet tells you to check.

risks.t: Sticky steering that won't self-centre
risks.b: By far the most-reported problem on this car. Owners describe the wheel catching or feeling notchy during small corrections at speed, then not returning to centre on its own. It makes lane-keeping tiring and it does not fix itself.
e: 97 steering complaints — the single largest category for this model year.
Filings describe needing constant two-handed correction and overcorrecting on the highway.
Drive it on a real road at 60 mph, not around the block. This is invisible in a parking lot and obvious in a lane.

risks.t: Fuel pump failure — stalls without warning
risks.b: Low-density impellers in the fuel pump can deform and kill the pump. Cars stall in traffic. There is a recall, but owners have reported waiting months for parts.
e: 78 fuel and propulsion complaints, second only to steering.
Filings state the impeller was improperly moulded and can render the pump inoperative over time.
Run the VIN before you go. If the recall is open and unrepaired, that is a stall risk you are inheriting, not a discount.

risks.t: Sunroof glass shattering on its own
risks.b: A handful of filings describe the sunroof spontaneously shattering with no impact during normal driving. Rare, but it is in the federal record rather than just forum folklore.
e: Reported under the Unknown or Other category alongside AC compressor failures.
Not a reason to walk. Worth knowing it is real if it happens to you.

chk: Drive it at highway speed for at least 15 minutes. The steering complaint is the number one issue on this car and it does not show up below 40 mph.
Run the VIN for the fuel pump recall. Free to fix, and an open one means the car can stall in traffic.
Make small steering corrections and let go. The wheel should return to centre by itself. If you have to bring it back, that is the fault owners are describing.
Ask whether the steering has already been serviced. Some cars were addressed under warranty. Paperwork here is worth money.

meta.title: 2019 Honda Civic Problems: Steering, Not the Engine
meta.desc: 348 federal complaints on the 2019 Civic and the biggest cluster is steering — 97 filings about a wheel that sticks and won't self-centre. Plus a fuel pump recall. What to test and what it costs.

camry_2018.name: 2018 Toyota Camry
camry_2018.vline: The most reliable car in America has a transmission problem.
camry_2018.vsub: 726 complaints on the 2018 Camry, and 289 of them — nearly two in five — are the powertrain. Owners describe harsh shifting, RPM flaring to 4,000 between gears, and in several filings burnt fluid with clutch material in it. This is the car everyone buys because nothing goes wrong with it. Something goes wrong with this one.

risks.t: 8-speed transmission — flaring, jerking, rebuilds
risks.b: The dominant complaint on this car and it is not close. Filings describe jerking and sputtering with loss of acceleration at highway speed, harsh engagement after the revs flare, and complete rebuilds. One filing reports burnt fluid carrying clutch pack material at 53,000 miles.
e: 289 power train complaints out of 726 total — 40% of everything filed against this model year.
Filings describe RPM flare to 4,000 between gears before hard engagement.
This is the entire inspection. A Camry that shifts cleanly through traffic is the car you wanted. One that flares is a five-figure car with a four-figure repair waiting.

risks.t: Brake pedal going hard, low-pressure warnings
risks.b: Owners report the pedal suddenly becoming hard to press while driving, and a “brake pressure low” warning, with brake pump and booster replacement as the fix.
e: 42 hydraulic service brake complaints for this model year.
Rare compared to the transmission, but this one is a safety item rather than an annoyance. Ask directly whether the booster has been touched.

risks.t: Steering stiffening and not returning to centre
risks.b: A smaller cluster describing steering that catches and is hard to bring back to centre, most noticeable at lower speeds.
e: 23 steering complaints filed for the 2018 model year.
Worth two minutes in a parking lot. Not worth walking away over on its own.

chk: Drive it 30 minutes in stop-and-go traffic. The transmission is 40% of every complaint on this car and it misbehaves under load and light throttle, not on a smooth highway.
Watch the tachometer between gears. Revs climbing before the gear engages is the exact fault owners describe. Once is enough to know.
Ask for transmission service records. Fluid changed on schedule matters here more than it does on most Toyotas.
Press the brake pedal firmly at a stop before you drive off. Owners report it going hard without warning. It should feel consistent.

meta.title: 2018 Toyota Camry Problems: 289 of 726 Complaints Are the Transmission
meta.desc: The 2018 Camry has 726 federal complaints and 40% of them are the 8-speed transmission — RPM flare, harsh engagement, rebuilds. What to drive for and what a repair costs.

crv_2019.name: 2019 Honda CR-V
crv_2019.vline: 1,074 complaints. America's favourite SUV has a bad year.
crv_2019.vsub: This is one of the most-complained-about vehicles of its generation, and the pattern mirrors the Civic it shares parts with: 128 steering filings about a wheel that sticks and won't self-centre, and 89 fuel system filings including pumps that quit in traffic. Popular does not mean problem-free — it means more owners filing.

risks.t: Fuel pump failure — stalling in traffic
risks.b: Owners report the car stalling outright and having to roll out of an intersection. Filings describe confirmed pump failure at independent shops. There is recall coverage, so the VIN check is the whole game here.
e: 89 fuel and propulsion complaints on this model year.
One filing describes stalling in an intersection and rolling the car clear of traffic.
An unrepaired recall on a car that stalls is not a bargaining chip, it is a reason to make them fix it before you take delivery.

risks.t: Steering sticks and won't return to centre
risks.b: The single largest category. Owners describe notchiness on small corrections and a wheel that has to be manually brought back to centre. Same complaint pattern as the Civic of the same year.
e: 128 steering complaints — more than any other component on this vehicle.
Test it on a highway, not a test loop. It is the most common thing wrong with this car and the easiest to miss.

risks.t: Collision avoidance false alarms
risks.b: Filings describe the forward collision system braking or warning with nothing there. Annoying rather than dangerous, but it wears on you daily.
e: 31 forward collision avoidance complaints for this model year.
Ask the seller directly. Owners who have it usually volunteer it, because it is impossible to ignore.

chk: Run the VIN for the fuel pump recall first. Cars stalling in intersections is in the federal record. If it is open, make them complete it before money changes hands.
Fifteen minutes at highway speed, hands light on the wheel. The steering fault is the top complaint and only shows up above about 40 mph.
Ask whether the collision system has ever braked for nothing. 31 owners filed about it. The seller will know.
Don't read the complaint count as a verdict. This is a best-seller, so more owners file. Compare the pattern, not the total.

meta.title: 2019 Honda CR-V Problems: 1,074 Complaints, Led by Steering and Fuel Pumps
meta.desc: The 2019 CR-V has 1,074 federal complaints — 128 about steering that sticks, 89 about fuel pumps that stall the car. What to test drive for and which recall to check.

grandcherokee_2017.name: 2017 Jeep Grand Cherokee
grandcherokee_2017.vline: Two expensive systems, and both of them are in the top two.
grandcherokee_2017.vsub: 361 complaints, and the top two categories are the two that cost the most to fix: 89 powertrain and 78 engine. Owners describe transfer cases failing, and camshafts destroyed with metal circulating through the engine at 90,000 miles. This is not a car where the common problems are cheap ones.

risks.t: Camshaft failure with metal through the engine
risks.b: Filings describe a ticking noise that turns out to be destroyed camshafts, with metal debris distributed through the rest of the engine. One owner reports it at 90,881 miles. Another describes an oil cooler failure cascading into head gaskets and then a whole engine at 103,000.
e: 78 engine complaints on this model year, second only to powertrain.
Filings quote camshafts destroyed with metal throughout the engine at just over 90,000 miles.
A ticking noise on this engine is not a tappet you live with. Walk unless a specialist has been inside it and says otherwise.

risks.t: Transfer case and driveline failure
risks.b: The largest category. Owners report a flashing Service 4WD warning at speed followed by transfer case replacement, and in one filing a loud bang and grinding from a stop, after which the vehicle shifted itself to neutral and would not move.
e: 89 power train complaints — the top category for this model year.
Drive it in 4WD, and drive it from a dead stop under load. Both failures in the filings show up exactly there.

risks.t: Electrical gremlins
risks.b: A steady stream of electrical filings on top of the mechanical ones. Individually small, collectively the reason a lot of these get sold.
e: 35 electrical system complaints for this model year.
Sit in it and press every button before you drive it. Ten minutes now saves a year of small annoyances.

chk: Start it cold and listen for ticking. On this engine that noise is in 78 federal filings and it ends in a four-figure bill or a new engine.
Get an oil analysis, or at minimum look at the oil. Owners found metal circulating before the engine let go. It is the only early warning.
Engage 4WD and drive from a dead stop under load. Transfer case failures in the filings appear exactly under those conditions.
Budget for this car, not just buy it. The two most common problems here are both four-figure repairs. That has to be in your number before you offer.

meta.title: 2017 Jeep Grand Cherokee Problems: The Two Most Common Are Also the Most Expensive
meta.desc: 361 federal complaints on the 2017 Grand Cherokee. 89 powertrain, 78 engine — destroyed camshafts, metal through the engine, transfer case failures. What to check before you buy.
